blocks.text: Backward Elimination genuinely tested every currently included feature for possible removal at each round, training a separate model for every single candidate, a real, direct but genuinely expensive process. Recursive feature elimination refines that exact same backward direction into something considerably more efficient, training only one model per round and using that model own internal feature ranking directly to decide what to remove.

This topic covers the key, genuine efficiency difference between recursive feature elimination and plain backward elimination, the step by step process this technique actually follows, the step parameter that controls how many features get removed per round, the real, genuine requirement that the underlying model must expose its own feature ranking, and RFECV, the variant that automatically finds the optimal number of features rather than requiring it to be specified in advance.
1. The Key, Genuine Efficiency Difference
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443421903-872948153.png

Plain backward elimination, covered in the previous topic, genuinely trains a separate model for every single feature currently in the set, just to figure out which one removal hurts performance least. Recursive feature elimination genuinely skips that entire, expensive process, training just one single model on the current feature set, then directly reading that model own internal ranking of feature importance to decide what to remove.

This is genuinely the single most important idea in this entire topic, rather than empirically testing every possible removal through repeated retraining, RFE trusts the model own, already computed internal signal, coefficients for a linear model, importance scores for a tree based model, to make that same decision directly and considerably faster.
2. The Step by Step Process
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443421904-496155122.png

At each round, RFE genuinely trains one model on the current feature set, ranks every feature currently included by that model own coefficients or importance scores, and removes the single genuinely least important feature directly, based on that ranking. This entire genuine process then repeats on the smaller, remaining feature set, round after round, until the target feature count is reached.

This is genuinely a real, direct application of the feature importance concept, previewed briefly here and covered in full depth in the Feature Importance topic that closes out this entire module, RFE uses that exact same underlying idea, applied repeatedly, as its actual selection mechanism.
3. A Worked Example
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443421904-887791546.png
Using scikit-learn RFE directly shows this efficient, model ranking driven process in action, on the exact same dataset used in the previous two topics.

code.content:
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import RFE
import pandas as pd

X = pd.DataFrame({
    "square_feet": [900, 1200, 1500, 1800, 2100, 2400],
    "bedrooms": [2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5],
    "shoe_size_unrelated": [8, 9, 7, 10, 8, 9],
})
y = pd.Series([0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1])

rfe = RFE(LogisticRegression(), n_features_to_select=2, step=1)
rfe.fit(X, y)

print("Selected features:", X.columns[rfe.support_].tolist())
print("Feature ranking:", rfe.ranking_)

blocks.text: RFE genuinely arrives at the same square_feet and bedrooms result as both previous topics, but does so training genuinely far fewer models along the way, relying on the logistic regression own coefficient magnitudes to directly identify shoe_size_unrelated as the genuinely least important feature to remove.

blocks.title: A practical habit
blocks.content: Check rfe.ranking_ directly after fitting, not just the final selected features. It genuinely shows the full order features were removed in, useful context for understanding the search result.

blocks.text: 4. Controlling the Step Size
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443421904-30673099.png

The step parameter genuinely controls how many features get removed at once per round, the default, step equals 1, removes exactly one feature per round, the genuinely most precise, careful option. Setting step to a genuinely larger number removes several of the lowest ranked features at once each round, trading some genuine precision for additional real speed.

This is a genuinely useful, practical knob for datasets with a very large number of features, where even RFE genuine one model per round efficiency can still add up to a real, meaningful amount of computation across many rounds.

blocks.text: 5. The Real Requirement: A Model That Exposes Its Own Ranking

blocks.alt: The Real Requirement: A Model That Exposes Its Own Ranking
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443421905-521989629.png

Recursive feature elimination genuinely only works with models that expose either coef_, for linear models, or feature_importances_, for tree based models, since that internal ranking is exactly what drives every single removal decision. A plain K-nearest neighbors model, which genuinely has no such internal ranking at all, simply looking up nearby points directly, cannot be used with RFE in this direct way.

This is genuinely the same kind of real, practical model support limitation first covered back in Class Weighting, a genuinely powerful technique that nonetheless depends on a specific capability not every model actually provides.

blocks.title: Worth remembering
blocks.content: Before reaching for RFE, genuinely confirm the chosen model exposes coef_ or feature_importances_. This same real requirement echoes the model support limitation first covered back in Class Weighting.

blocks.text: 6. RFECV: Automatically Finding the Right Feature Count

blocks.alt: RFECV: Automatically Finding the Right Feature Count
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443422143-564194688.png

Plain RFE genuinely requires specifying n_features_to_select manually in advance, exactly as in the worked example above. RFECV removes that genuine requirement entirely, using cross validation to automatically test different feature counts and select whichever genuinely produces the best real, cross validated performance, answering the how many features question directly rather than leaving it to a manual guess.

This is genuinely a real, practical improvement worth reaching for whenever the right number of features to keep is not already clearly known, letting the data itself, evaluated honestly through cross validation, make that genuine determination.

blocks.text: 7. The Real Efficiency Payoff
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443422145-331310303.png

Plain backward elimination genuinely trains roughly n squared over 2 models in total across its entire run, testing every removal candidate at every round. Recursive feature elimination genuinely trains only about n models total, one per round, a real, substantial, genuine efficiency gain that grows considerably more pronounced as the number of features increases.

This real, genuine efficiency is exactly why RFE, and specifically RFECV, are often the genuinely preferred, practical choice over plain backward elimination in real projects, delivering a closely related, model informed selection at a real fraction of the total computational cost.
8. Recursive Feature Elimination Versus What Comes Next

Forward Selection, Backward Elimination, and Recursive Feature Elimination together complete this module second family, wrapper methods, real model performance driving selection, refined here into a genuinely efficient, practical technique by directly using a model own internal feature ranking.
